transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
More reports of computer outages today,
this time from NSA and Apple.
Here's NPR's Greg Myrie.
>> Apple users reported problems
with both the App Store and Apple Pay.
At the National Security Agency,
the nation's largest intelligence agency,
an internal communications network went down.
The agency said this happened
during scheduled routine maintenance,
adding that, quote, "mission-critical capabilities
were not affected."
These are the latest in a series
of seemingly unrelated computer outages in recent days.
They've included Microsoft, major banks,
and the Federal Aviation Administration.
Computer experts say there's no indication
these organizations have been hacked.
Rather, they say, the computer networks appear to be going down
as they are being patched or upgraded.
Greg Myrie, NPR News, Washington.
>> In his first public statement
since resigning from NVIDIA last week,
former CEO Jensen Wong is striking a remorseful tone
over controversies that prompted him to step down.
He admitted to having extramarital affairs,
including with a woman suspected of spying for China.
But some members of the tech world
are lobbying to get Wong reinstated
to the helm of the chipmaker at the heart of the AI boom.
And Wong says he'll return if the board lets him.
After the market closes,
NVIDIA will release its third-quarter earnings.
President Trump suggested he may raise the NVIDIA scandal
with Chinese leader Xi Jinping
when they and Russian leader Vladimir Putin
hold their historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen this week.
And Piers Frank Ordonez reports on what is on the agenda.
>> Trump wants to make progress on nuclear arms control,
and he also wants help with Iran.
But China actually has shown very little interest
in reducing their nuclear weapons,
and we'll see if she would take any steps
to put more pressure on Iran, which he hasn't yet.
>> NPR's Frank Ordonez.
After 26 years, the U.S. has lost its measles-free status,
according to the Pan American Health Organization.
The announcement comes as the country is reporting
more than 5,400 cases with 10 associated deaths.
More from NPR's Maria Godoy.
>> The determination means that measles
is once again spreading regularly in the U.S.
Measles is incredibly contagious.
High vaccination rates of at least 95%
are needed to stop its spread.
Since the pandemic, childhood vaccination rates
have fallen below that threshold,
allowing outbreaks to take hold.
In the coming weeks, the U.S. is expected to submit a plan
to the organization on how it plans
to once again get measles under control.
Dr. Rhonda Seeley-Thomas with the Pan American Group
says that would require increasing vaccination rates,
improving surveillance, and having a rapid-response plan.
>> Human and financial resources are required for this.
>> Meanwhile, health departments across the U.S.
are already struggling with funding and staffing cuts.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
>> It's NPR.
The Federal Aviation Administration
has paused the installation of Juniper Router,
similar to that which played a role
in Friday's nationwide air ground stop.
This from an FAA official requested anonymity
because they're not authorized to speak publicly.
Last week, the FAA's aging systems were overwhelmed
after L3 Harris employees converted legacy
but unsupported copper wires to a modern fiber optic system
and installed a new router in El Dorado, Arkansas,
flooding the FAA network with excess data.
Amid anxiety about the future of work,
NPR's Andrea Shue reports apprenticeships
in the skilled trades are having a moment.
>> When Trent Parker first became instruction coordinator
for the Electrical Trade Center in Columbus, Ohio,
he encountered a high school administrator
who thought the center's apprenticeship program
would be appropriate for kids who were flunking out.
Now, with AI threatening many white-collar professions,
Parker has seen how the trades have become highly attractive
to people of all backgrounds,
including those who went to college.
>> You can see it and feel it. You talk with parents.
The word is out that college is not the only way to go,
that there are other alternatives.
>> Alternatives that guarantee work.
Enrollment in his apprenticeship has soared in recent years
as demand for electricians has grown.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
>> Golf icon Tiger Woods is returning to competition
next month at a PGA tournament in the Bahamas.
This will be his first since he was charged
with driving under the influence
when he crashed his car in Florida earlier this year.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
>> This message comes from GiveWell,
a research and grant-making organization
focused on finding cost-effective ways
to help save and improve lives.
Find out more or make a tax-deductible donation today
at GiveWell.org.
Select podcast and NPR at checkout.

topics.text: Apple users report App Store and Apple Pay problems; NSA internal network goes down during maintenance
Jensen Huang apologizes for affairs, including one with suspected Chinese spy, after NVIDIA resignation
Trump may raise NVIDIA scandal with Xi Jinping at Shenzhen trilateral meeting with Putin
US loses measles-free status after 26 years, with over 5,400 cases and 10 deaths
FAA pauses installation of Juniper router linked to nationwide air ground stop
Skilled trade apprenticeships surge as AI threatens white-collar jobs, Columbus electrical program grows
Tiger Woods returns to competition next month at PGA tournament in the Bahamas after DUI charge
